title: new01
live_proof: verified in the pin on 2026-10-16, by reading the three sites and by measurement. The JEACH_JSON arm of jsonEachColumn does sqlite3_result_text(ctx, p->sParse.zJson, -1, SQLITE_STATIC); jsonEachFilter allocates p->zJson with sqlite3_malloc64 and hands it to jsonParse, which is what makes p->sParse.zJson that same buffer; jsonEachCursorReset frees it. Host ASan: heap-use-after-free, 0 bytes inside a freed 8-byte region, read by memcmp under binCollFunc (sqlite3.c:144244) <- vdbeCompareMemString <- sqlite3MemCompare <- minmaxStep, freed by sqlite3_free <- jsonEachCursorReset at sqlite3.c:185489, allocated by sqlite3_malloc64 <- jsonEachFilter at sqlite3.c:185749. Those two line numbers are what separate this case from case 16 in the measurement rather than in prose: 16's buffer is freed at :185490 and allocated at :185771, one and twenty-two lines away, because it is p->zRoot from the default arm. Fixed upstream in 3.45.2 by switching this arm to SQLITE_TRANSIENT
object: p->zJson, the cursor's own malloc'd copy of the input JSON, handed to the SQL layer as SQLITE_STATIC
lifetime_ender: driving json_each from the right of a join re-filters it per outer row, and each jsonEachFilter calls jsonEachCursorReset, freeing the previous zJson
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator. The accumulator is the part that makes it observable: SQLITE_STATIC means no copy is made and sqlite3VdbeMemCopy keeps MEM_Static as-is, so a min()/max() accumulator retains the raw pointer and minmaxStep() compares against freed memory. Built in the json group

fault_sites_why: minmaxStep compares against the freed zJson through binCollFunc, whose byte compare is memcmp, and the runners resolve only the faulting pc's symbol. Declared 2026-10-10 after the virtual runs resolved faults there, which is weaker than a pre-declaration, and the old text said so: any memcmp under this case would count. STRENGTHENED 2026-10-16 by probe site 53, which prints the pointer at the SQLITE_STATIC hand-out, at the free in jsonEachCursorReset and at every comparison: the pointer the accumulator keeps is the pointer the reset frees, and three comparisons follow that free on native memsys5, on virtual Capstone with lookaside off and on CheriBSD purecap alike. What the probe cannot do here is separate the dead pointer from the live one by address, for the reason in the note -- which is itself the point of the case
note: Re-measured 2026-10-16; every verdict holds, and the probe turned up the sharpest evidence in this corpus for judging by identity rather than by address or by value. Probe site 53 shows the same sequence on all three platforms: RESET frees zJson p=X, then the next cursor's jsonEachFilter hands out zJson at the SAME address X with the SAME content ([3,4,5], since the trigger re-filters the same inner table), and then three comparisons read X. So the accumulator's dead pointer and the live buffer coincide in address and in bytes: an address oracle cannot see the access (witnesses=0, hits=14), a value check cannot either because the bytes are the ones the comparison expected, and the result of the comparison is correct by accident. Host ASan sees it only because its quarantine refuses to reissue the block. Sublet rejects it with cause 25 because the accumulator holds a capability that was revoked at the free, while the new cursor holds a different child covering the same bytes -- the one distinction that survives when address and content do not. Case 16, the sibling, happened to have its block reissued elsewhere, which is why its stale operand was separable by address there and is not here
